reasons_add: Al-Damghani glosses asfara as dawn brightening and becoming clear. Al-Suyuti's Itqan reports a proposed etymology of tafsir from reversed safar, illustrated by dawn brightening; he also reports derivations from fasr and a physician's diagnostic test.

In his opening praise, al-Suyuti metaphorically calls the Prophet's truthful dawn the light that erased deviation and wrongdoing. Bint al-Shati says the physical degrees of light and dark in oaths by dawn, sun, and night clarify guidance and truth versus error and falsehood.
Bint al-Shati also invokes 89:1, 93:1, 92:1, and 53:1 when discussing oaths by dawn, sun, and night and their light-dark imagery.

question: 74:34/q08
position: The oath-waw directs attention to perceptible realities that cannot be disputed, preparing for disputed abstractions or unseen truths.
reasons: Bint al-Shati prefers this rhetorical account over the common claim that the oath-waw only magnifies what is sworn by; she cites 10:5, 6:96, 10:67, 27:86, 3:190, 45:5, 25:47, and 30:23 as sensory parallels.

positions.position: Al-Damghani also lists senses of saqat: regret, falling into shirk, scattering, and literal falling.
positions.reasons: Al-Damghani gives this separate lexical entry alongside the extracted dawn gloss.

positions.position: Al-Suyuti explains the abridgment, title, and prayer attached to his report collection.
positions.reasons: Al-Suyuti says he condensed his multivolume isnad-based Tafsir Musnad to provide hadith texts without long chains while retaining text and reliable-book references. He titles it al-Durr al-manthur fi al-tafsir bi-l-ma'thur and asks God to guard its author against error and falsehood.

positions.position: The collection gives reports about al-Fatihah's Qur'anic status, codex inclusion, and Meccan revelation.
positions.reasons: Ibrahim reports al-Aswad's affirmation that al-Fatihah is Qur'an, transmitted by Abd ibn Humayd. Reports from Muhammad ibn Sirin and Ibn al-Anbari say Ubayy wrote al-Fatihah, the two protective suras, and invocations whereas Ibn Masud wrote none. Uthman wrote al-Fatihah and the protective suras; Ibn Masud said he would have placed al-Fatihah at the beginning of everything had he written it. Ali says it came down in Mecca from a treasure beneath the Throne, transmitted by al-Wahidi and al-Tha'labi.

positions.position: Abu Maysarah reports the Prophet's account to Khadijah of hearing a voice while alone.
positions.reasons: Abu Maysarah Amr ibn Shurahbil says the Prophet feared what the voice meant and Khadijah answered, 'God forbid.'

positions.position: The Itqan reports derivations and differing definitions of tafsir and ta'wil.
positions.reasons: Al-Suyuti reports ta'wil derived from return or governance. Abu Ubayd and others identify tafsir with ta'wil; Ibn Habib objects to treating them as synonyms. Al-Raghib calls tafsir broader and word-focused, ta'wil meaning- and sentence-focused. Other accounts distinguish a word with one sense from choosing among several by evidence, or categorical divine intent from ranked possibilities (al-Maturidi), or lexical evidence from inward intended reality (Abu Talib al-Taghlibi, with his watchful-ambush example).
